# Karryam Vendor — splash, onboarding and authentication designs

Open `index.html` in a browser for the full screen gallery. Choose **Play onboarding prototype** for the interactive journey. Individual screens use `?mode=phone&screen=SCREEN_ID` for an exact, borderless export. This is a local design deliverable, not the Flutter implementation or a live authentication client.

## Dimensions and layout

- Primary artboards: **393 × 852 logical pixels**, a realistic modern phone viewport. These are app design points, not a device’s physical pixel resolution.
- Top system area: 54 px; bottom home area: 34 px. System indicators are illustrative and must be provided by the OS in the implemented app.
- Horizontal margins: 24 px; actions: 56 px tall; minimum control touch area: 44 px. Keyboard screens must resize/scroll around the actual OS keyboard.
- Phone preview adapts to 360 × 800 and 375 × 812; large text should use scrolling rather than truncate fields or actions.
- Components: primary/secondary action, compact original-logo plate, field, method tabs, OTP field, vendor selector, recovery notice, progress dots and status illustrations.
- Onboarding supports Skip, visible progress and a direct Sign in route. The tour is optional and local; its completion is not business verification.

## Brand authority

Reviewed user-supplied `Karryam_Landing_Page.pdf`, including its visual, motion, accessibility and merchant sections. Also reviewed the colocated `Karryam_Brand_Guidelines.pdf` (38 pages) for exact product design rules.

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| brand.navy.900 | #0B1F44 | Dark surfaces, headings, primary light-surface actions |
| brand.teal.500 | #00C2A8 | Progress, selected emphasis, dark-surface actions, routes |
| brand.white | #FFFFFF | Light surfaces and dark-surface text |
| brand.gray.400 | #A7B0BB | Secondary dark-surface metadata |
| brand.indigo.700 | #2D3A5B | Readable supporting text |
| teal tint 10% | #E6F9F6 | Quiet illustration and notice surfaces |
| navy tint 10% | #E7E9EC | Quiet neutral separation |
| text.link | #007D6D | Readable darkened teal for small text on white |

Inter is bundled locally so previews work offline. Font license is included. Error colours are semantic UI states, as permitted by the brand guidelines. Teal is not normal body text on white. Light screens use navy primary buttons with white labels; dark onboarding uses teal buttons with navy labels.

The original logo is copied intact from `web/karryam-landing/public/images/logo.png`; it matches the supplied logo image. No redraw, recolour, effects or geometry edits. The transparent white-wordmark lockup sits on quiet navy surfaces. The 128 px header lockup exceeds the 120 px minimum, with at least 0.25 × symbol-height clear space. The splash uses a 252 px lockup. Product descriptor and CosmicForge endorsement remain separate and secondary.

## Screen inventory

1. Splash — restores local session / starts app; the 1.2 s demo transition is illustrative, never a production minimum wait.
2. Welcome — merchant photography and business value.
3. Catalogue — Food and Shop shown as distinct contexts.
4. Fulfilment — overview of order preparation and enabled handover.
5. Sign in by phone.
6. Sign in by email.
7. Phone code verification.
8. Email code verification.
9. Conditional vendor account choice.
10. Authentication complete — ends this design set.
11. Invalid code.
12. Expired code.
13. Verification in progress — action disabled to prevent duplicate submission.
14. Connection recovery.
15. No active vendor access.
16. Suspended access.

Screen images and a printable design PDF are generated by `verify_design.py`. `screens/overview.png` shows the first nine screens together. Screens are also exported individually at 393 × 852.

## Exact backend mapping

Authoritative source: `services/vendor-service/internal/features/auth/http/dto.go`, `http/handler.go`, `usecases/auth_service.go`, `shared/go/auth/otp.go`, and the existing `apps/vendor/lib/features/auth` foundation.

| Screen / action | Contract |
|---|---|
| Send code | POST `/api/v1/vendor/auth/start`; exactly one of `phone` or `email` |
| Code expiry | `expires_in` from start/resend, not a hardcoded duration |
| Verify code | POST `/api/v1/vendor/auth/verify`; same identifier, `challenge_id`, `otp`; optional established `device_id` |
| Resend | POST `/api/v1/vendor/auth/resend`; same identifier and `challenge_id`; backend limits and any Retry-After govern availability |
| Choose vendor | Only for `requires_vendor_choice=true`; select from `available_vendor_ids`, then repeat verification with the same OTP/challenge plus `vendor_id` |
| Successful sign-in | Access/refresh token response; save using existing secure session store |
| Returning authenticated user | Session restoration/refresh, skip intro/auth when session is valid |
| No active affiliation / suspended affiliation | Backend 403; display returned access message; no retry loop |
| Invalid/expired code | Backend auth error; show readable message and allow correction/new code as appropriate |

The source uses six-digit login codes. OTP is one accessible input with six visual cells, supports numeric keyboard, paste and OS autofill, and never displays `debug_otp`. The demo accepts any six digits solely to navigate the designs. It performs **no network requests**, creates no accounts, and stores no credentials. Its in-memory input values clear on page close. Example contacts, 04:59 timer and two UUID vendor IDs are fixtures; they are not real account data or a production expiry policy. The demo exercises the multi-vendor branch; production single-vendor verification goes directly to successful authentication.

Auth exposes vendor IDs, not vendor display names, logos, branch names or staff roles. The selector therefore shows IDs. Adding friendlier account labels needs an authoritative backend response; do not invent them. Business owner/self-registration is not established by these contracts, so no Create account, password, social login, name, address or business setup form is introduced here. No separate marketing consent, referral rewards, fake order metrics, or notification/location permission prompt is added.

Connection recovery must preserve the identifier and challenge in transient memory and retry the failed operation explicitly. Recovery behaviour depends on which operation failed. Codes remain transient; do not write them to storage. Resend must not invent a client cooldown or claim delivery before the request succeeds. Production code may paste/autofill digits but must still use backend verification. Do not treat local demo navigation as successful authentication.

Business onboarding/verification (documents, bank, location and other enabled dimensions) is distinct from this introductory onboarding. It will require its own scoped design pass using the exact existing contracts. Dashboard is expressly excluded.

## Assets and motion

- `assets/karryam-logo.png`: exact existing official logo, copied intact.
- `assets/food.png`, `assets/shop.png`: existing Karryam landing imagery, copied intact.
- `assets/vendor-welcome.png`: custom AI-generated editorial merchant photograph, created with the built-in image generation tool. This is illustrative brand imagery, not a photograph of an actual merchant or testimonial.
- Secure handover / catalogue diagrams and outline icons are editable, code-native SVG/CSS; they are illustrative concepts and contain no fabricated live metrics.
- `IMAGE_PROMPT.md`: exact generation prompt and provenance.
- Inter Regular/Bold: official Google Fonts assets, locally bundled with SIL Open Font License.

Transitions: 180–240 ms for actions/screen changes in implementation. Progress should communicate actual work. Intro route motion may trace once, then settle. Reduced-motion users receive static artwork / immediate transitions. Logo never receives glow or decoration. No infinite ornamental motion beyond a temporary activity indicator.

Review validation is recorded in `VALIDATION.md`. Flutter widgets and backend wiring remain in the next implementation step.

## Re-rendering

Optional verification dependencies: Python `playwright`, `Pillow`, `pypdf`, plus installed Chrome. Run `python verify_design.py` from this directory to regenerate screenshots, PDF and checks. Viewing the preview itself needs only a browser; all fonts and images are bundled locally.
